transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because I've been having some trouble just... staying in my chair. 

Like during staff meetings, or even at dinner. I just keep getting up when everyone else is seated. I'll suddenly go refill my coffee, or walk to the back of the room to check a handout... even though nothing is really urgent. I just... I get up.
When you get up like that, do you feel an inner urge or restlessness that builds until you move?

I suppose you could say that. Um... I just don't really stop. 

Especially lately. Since my youngest left for college, the house has been a lot quieter, and I just find myself constantly doing something. I'll go straight from lesson planning to... doing the laundry, then out to softball practice, or chopping food for a community event. I don't really pause. Even on the nights I promise myself I'm just going to sit down and rest... I don't. I just keep moving.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different things most days?
No... not really. I mean, I have normal things to think about, but I wouldn't say I'm sitting around worrying about them. I just prefer to keep busy.
Did these difficulties with restlessness and staying seated start when you were a child?

I suppose so. Um... looking back, even as a girl, my report cards usually said I was bright, but... that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. My mother used to joke that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. So... yes. It's not exactly new.
When you’re working on something, do you often have trouble keeping your attention on it?
No, I wouldn't say so. Um... if I have something to do, I just do it. I don't really have trouble focusing on it.
Do you often lose track of what you’re doing or make careless mistakes because your mind wanders?
No... I don't think so. I don't really make careless mistakes. Um... I keep track of what I'm doing just fine.
Do you often act without thinking first, even when you know you probably should stop and consider it?
No, not really. I mean... I usually think things through. I don't just jump into things without considering them first.
When you’re sitting still, do you feel physically restless or like you have to move?

Well... I suppose a little. Um... if I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or... in church, maybe. I'll catch myself tapping my foot, or clicking my pen. Just... shifting around. I usually just have to remind myself to settle down. But... that's about it.
Do you often find yourself feeling worried or anxious about many different things most days?
No, I wouldn't say that. Um... just the normal amount, I suppose. I don't really spend my days worrying about things.
Do you often have trouble paying close attention to details or make careless mistakes when doing tasks?
No, not really. Um... I have to pay pretty close attention to things, grading papers and all. So... no, I don't think I make careless mistakes.
Have these restlessness and getting-up habits been present in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?
Well... I don't really think so. Um... at home, I just go about my evening, so I haven't really noticed it there. Just... what I mentioned before. I wouldn't call it a habit.
Have these restlessness and getting-up habits caused problems for you at work, at home, or in your relationships?

I suppose... well, it has caused some friction. People tend to lose patience with me when I can't just sit still. It happens at staff meetings... and at my book club. I end up just feeling a bit embarrassed about it all, rather than enjoying the time with them.
When you were a child, did teachers or family members say you had trouble paying attention or seemed easily distracted?

Well... I don't know about distracted, exactly. Um... my report cards back then usually said I was bright, but... that I just couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn, I suppose. My mother used to joke about it... she'd say I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. But... yes, I suppose that was something they noticed.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention when reading, listening, or doing tasks?
I don't think so, no. I mean... I read quite a lot. And I can listen just fine when I need to. I don't really have a problem focusing on things like that.
Do you often lose track of what you're doing because your mind wanders?
No... I wouldn't say so. My mind doesn't really wander like that. I usually know what I'm supposed to be doing.
Do you notice this restlessness in more than one setting, such as both at work and at home?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't paid much attention to that, to be honest. I suppose I haven't really noticed.
Do you often leave tasks unfinished because you get sidetracked?
No, I don't think so. I usually finish what I start.
Do you find that this need to get up and move around happens in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?
Not really. I mean... I'm on my feet a lot at the school anyway, but I wouldn't say I feel some sort of need to keep moving when I'm at home. I haven't really noticed anything unusual.
Do you feel restless or like you need to keep moving most days?

I suppose I stay pretty busy. Um... since the house got quieter, you know, after my youngest left for college... I just kind of keep going. I'll go from lesson planning to, I don't know, throwing in some laundry, then softball practice, and then chopping food for some community event. I don't really pause much. Even on the nights I tell myself I'm just going to rest. I just... keep doing things.
Did this restlessness and need to keep moving start before you were 12 years old?

I suppose so. Um... my mother used to joke that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. And... well, my old report cards usually said I was bright, but that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. So... yes.
